original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Can batched Git blob reads speed up research_package.validate on identical source inventories while retaining exact provenance, SHA256, live-input and original-card checks?
scope_change_reason: Profile the exact source-pin validation stage of registered research replay, before any mathematical command; batch Git reads only if they dominate wall time.
bottleneck_link: Registered replay source validation runs for every contributed package. Less Git process overhead saves review time without changing any mathematical command or proof input.
stop_rule: One fixed source-inventory benchmark and one batch implementation; retain only with a measurable same-fixture speedup and all rejection controls. About 60 minutes total, final quarter for verification.
evidence: BENCHMARK-python312.json and BENCHMARK-python314.json contain all samples for identical 10-row and 130-row inventories; twelve failure controls and six positive controls pass. Existing onboarding suite passes all twelve tests on Python 3.12. No mathematical replay or new kappa.
author: Arham Tahir
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents.

open_questions.question: Does the measured source validation speedup also hold on Linux?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The registered replay workflow uses Linux runners.
open_questions.first_step: Run the fixed benchmark and negative controls on Python 3.12 Linux.
open_questions.blocked_by: Hosted execution has not yet been observed.

method_domain: One source validation stage; fixed synthetic inventories of 8 or 128 committed script inputs plus two provenance rows. Five alternating old/new timings per fixture per interpreter; no persistent cache.
predecessor_credit: Douglas Colkitt: package manifest, exact pins, separation of live inputs and provenance, and explicit replay workflow. Maxime Fleury and Antoine Olivier: gzip portability audit used during task triage.

overlap_check.limits: Remote PR scope is open PRs including drafts. Closed work is searched through local READMEs, TASK metadata and ledger only. No code diffs or arbitrary package files are searched. Recheck relevant heads before submission.
